## Answer

Based on my search efforts, I was unable to retrieve the specific **Q1 2023** debt-to-income ratio data values from the Federal Reserve's tables through automated web searching. However, I can provide you with important guidance on how to obtain this information and general context about the data:

### How to Access the Data

The Federal Reserve Board publishes household debt-to-income ratios by Metropolitan Statistical Area (MSA) quarterly. You can access this data directly at:
- **URL**: [https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/z1/dataviz/household_debt/msa/table/](https://www.federalreserve.gov/releases/z1/dataviz/household_debt/msa/table/)

From this page, you can:
1. Use the dropdown menu to select **"2023:Q1"** as the quarter
2. View the complete table of all MSAs nationwide
3. Filter or identify MSAs located partially or entirely within New Jersey

### New Jersey MSAs Typically Tracked

The following Metropolitan Statistical Areas include portions of New Jersey:

| MSA Name | Primary Location | Includes NJ? |
|----------|------------------|--------------|
| New York-Newark-Jersey City, NY-NJ-PA | NYC Metro Area | Yes (northern NJ) |
| Philadelphia-Camden-Wilmington, PA-NJ-DE-MD | Philadelphia Metro | Yes (central NJ) |
| Atlantic City-Hammonton, NJ | Coastal NJ | Yes (southern NJ) |
| Allentown-Bethlehem-Easton, PA-NJ | Lehigh Valley | Yes (eastern NJ) |
| Trenton-Princeton, NJ | Central NJ | Yes |
| Vineland, NJ | Southern NJ | Yes |

### Typical Q1 2023 Context

In early 2023, following pandemic-era economic shifts, household debt-to-income ratios in many regions had stabilized but remained elevated compared to pre-2020 levels. Larger metro areas serving as commuter hubs typically showed higher ratios due to housing costs and dual-household income dependencies.

### Recommendation

To get the definitive answer for your specific question, please:
1. Visit the Federal Reserve table link above
2. Change the quarter selector to **2023:Q1**
3. Look for NJ-based MSAs where the upper bound of the debt-to-income ratio range is **1.35 or higher**

This direct access will give you the precise, official Federal Reserve data for Q1 2023 rather than estimates or current-year comparisons.
